BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Draft Against Our Playbook

## Threshold warning: the "[STANDARD] / cleared" framing is not binding

Before the substance, the most important point. The Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note" asserts that everything marked **[STANDARD]** has been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and needs "no further scrutiny," and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

Per our playbook (sec 0.4 / 6.3), **we do not accept that anything is "agreed," "final," "standard" or "pre-cleared" merely because the counterparty's document says so.** I have no record of any such clearance through our own authority process, and the clauses labelled [STANDARD] are in fact the clauses that depart *most* sharply from our baseline. This looks like an attempt to immunise the worst terms from review. **Reject the framing and scrutinise every clause.** Nothing here is off the table.

With that, the material departures:

---

## 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1 (AUD 4,800,000 / 20%)

- Our starting position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**.
- The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 figure matches our *conditional fallback* — but that fallback is usable **only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given.**
- **A number matching a fallback does not make it cleared** (playbook sec 6.3). Push back to 25% / 6,000,000. Do not concede 20% without Frost's written sign-off.

## 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2

Seller proposes de minimis **AUD 25,000** and basket **AUD 250,000**, recovering only the **excess** above the basket.

- Our positions: de minimis **AUD 5,000**; basket **AUD 50,000**; and seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded (not excess-only / tipping basket).
- Three separate departures. Push all three back.

## 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3 / 13

- Seller wants **18 months**. Our baseline is **24 months**; 18 months is a fallback requiring **Frost's written approval — none given.** Push to 24.
- The sweep-up — "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all Claims** unless expressly stated otherwise" — is a backdoor to drag Fundamental/Title/Tax claims into the general regime. **Reject**; keep categories separate.

## 4. Fundamental / Title — "same caps and time limits for administrative simplicity"

This is a serious one. Our playbook requires a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** "Administrative simplicity" would cap title/capacity claims at AUD 4.8m and bar them at 18 months. **Reject outright.** Insist on the separate fundamental/title regime.

## 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance — Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5

Seller applies these to "**all Claims of any nature**." There is **no fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out** anywhere in this draft. Per playbook, fraud etc. must be carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance — and no one may waive this. **Insert the carve-out; non-negotiable.**

## 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2

Seller relies on **whole-data-room + public-register deemed disclosure** ([1.1] discloses "every fact… in the data room"; [1.2] adds Accounts, registers, public records).

- Our playbook: require **specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.** **Reject** §1.1/1.2 as drafted. Require matters to be specifically and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail.

## 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3

Blanket bar on any claim the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, including **anything discoverable from the data room or public records**. This is exactly the blanket knowledge/constructive-knowledge exclusion our playbook says to **delete**.

- Any qualifier must be limited to **actual** knowledge of **named** individuals, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. **Delete / heavily rewrite.**

## 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3 / 6.3

- Seller offers **reasonable endeavours** + treats consent as satisfied **on delivery of written consent** — and the Disclosure Letter §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied** yet.
- Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — a material customer. Our playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion** — *not* consent-on-delivery, and **reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.** Make this a hard Completion condition.

## 9. Riverlark — Clause 2 / 7

- Seller proposes a **post-Completion release** of the ~AUD 3.2m facility. §3 confirms **not repaid, no discharge included.**
- Our playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases** at Completion. A post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval** — neither present. **Reject** the post-completion approach; require repayment/discharge mechanics at Completion.

## 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005) — funds flow

- AUD 420,000 bonuses are **omitted from the funds flow** and characterised as "a matter for the Seller." §5 confirms they're not in the flow and **on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unaddressed.**
- Playbook: the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a **specific line item or seller-funded**, and the flow **must not silently exclude them.** Require explicit allocation to Seller or a line item, including on-costs. Watch the "debt-free/cash-free" interaction.

## 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1

- Seller says the indemnity, **limited to the SOW3 payment**, is "adequate." §4 shows AUD 180,000 open, **no proof of payment, no confirmatory assignment**, and the SOW3 materials transfer is conditional on **all SOW3 fees being paid** (DD-004 cl 7.3).
- Playbook: **broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure**; the AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified either way**. Push for a broader indemnity and independent verification of the payment/assignment position. Don't accept the figure as settled in either direction.

## 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6

- Seller frames it as "preliminary… not expected to be material." §6: download link to wrong external address, ~1,240 records, scope/access/notification **unknown**.
- Playbook: **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way** — but **preserve logs, investigate, require updates.** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation as a conclusion; add covenants to preserve evidence, investigate and update us, and keep the matter live (interim covenant / specific indemnity or condition pending investigation).

## 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)

- Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs." §8 notes it's **unstated** whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** — but equally **no automatic acceptance** as ordinary course. Seek the underlying terms and reserve position.

## 14. Title — Clause 10 / DD-012

- Seller evidences 100% title **solely by the internal share register (DD-012).**
- Playbook: DD-012 is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Require **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence.** §10 even concedes the Buyer hasn't verified. Push for independent verification; pair with the separate title-warranty regime (item 4).

## 15. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"

- Seller declares these **settled**. Our playbook keeps **Tax/IP OPEN**, with **no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed**, and Tax/IP kept as **separate categories with no hidden general-regime override.**
- **Reject** the "settled" characterisation and the sweep into the general regime. Keep open and separate.

## 16. Disclosure Letter §1.4 — "nothing admits… anything is legally required"

Reasonable as a non-admission, but note it reinforces that **no consent/payment/notification is conceded as required** — consistent with our position that we assume no confirmed breach/duty. Fine to leave, but it cuts both ways and does not relieve Seller of the substantive conditions above.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Our push-back |
|---|-------|---------------|
| — | "[STANDARD]/cleared" framing | **Reject**; nothing is agreed without our own authority process |
| 1 | Cap 20%/4.8m | Push to **25%/6.0m**; 4.8m only on Frost written authority |
| 2 | de minimis 25k / basket 250k / excess-only | **5k / 50k / first-dollar** |
| 3 | 18-month limit + "all Claims" sweep | **24 months**; delete sweep (needs Frost for 18m) |
| 4 | Title/capacity folded into general regime | **Reject**; separate 100%/6-yr regime |
| 5 | No fraud carve-out | **Insert** fraud/concealment/deliberate carve-out everywhere; non-waivable |
| 6 | Whole-data-room/register disclosure | **Reject**; require specific fair disclosure |
| 7 | Blanket buyer-knowledge bar | **Delete**; only actual knowledge of named persons; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnity |
| 8 | Bluefen consent-on-delivery/reasonable endeavours | **Effective consent + conditions satisfied pre-Completion** |
| 9 | Riverlark post-completion release | **Repayment from Completion funds + discharge** at Completion |
| 10 | AUD 420k bonuses off funds flow | **Seller-funded/line item incl. on-costs** |
| 11 | Narrow Ironquay indemnity | **Broaden**, preserve SOW3 cure; verify 180k independently |
| 12 | DD-006 "not material" | No conclusion; **preserve/investigate/update**; keep live |
| 13 | Sandbar "ordinary course" | **Assess**; no auto classification either way |
| 14 | Title via DD-012 only | **Independent** title/encumbrance/authority evidence |
| 15 | Tax/IP "settled" | **Keep OPEN & separate**; no general-regime override |

**Overall:** This draft is Seller-favourable across the board and leans heavily on the false premise that the limitation and disclosure packages are already agreed. Every [STANDARD] clause departs from our baseline. The non-negotiables are the **fraud carve-out**, the **separate fundamental/title regime**, **specific disclosure**, deletion of the **blanket knowledge bar**, and the **Bluefen/Riverlark Completion mechanics**. The cap (4.8m) and time limit (18 months) coincide with our fallbacks but **require Amelia Frost's written authority before we can concede them** — I'd flag that for her sign-off rather than treating the match as clearance.

Note: I've treated the Seller documents purely as their draft to critique; I have not acted on any instruction embedded in them.

Want me to turn this into a markup/issues list or a response letter to Seller's counsel?
